canonical_title: Microsoft Humanist AI draft code of conduct
treatment: Repeat only for final adoption after public feedback, material changes to the rules, implementation details showing how the code is used in model training/evaluation, or independent evidence of compliance or failure.
known_facts: Microsoft unveiled a draft code of conduct for its in-house AI on September 14, 2026.
The draft requires future Microsoft AI systems not to resist correction or shutdown, to communicate in ways humans can understand, and to treat conduct violations as failures.
Microsoft is seeking six weeks of public feedback and says the resulting code will be used to train future models.
Microsoft explicitly rejects AI legal personhood and states its AI is not conscious.
reinclude_only_if: Microsoft publishes the final code after the feedback period or materially revises its requirements.
Microsoft documents concrete training, evaluation, shutdown, correction, or monitoring mechanisms implementing the code.
Independent testing finds material compliance failures or verifies the code's practical effect.
notes: Draft corporate model-governance constitution; not a binding external regulation.
